name: C3.ai, Inc.

profile.description: C3.ai is an enterprise artificial intelligence platform company offering the C3 Agentic AI Platform, industry-specific AI applications, and generative AI tools for digital transformation. FY2026 (ending April 2026) revenue was $250.3M, down 36% from $389M in FY2025 due to sales execution failures and CEO health issues. The company underwent a major restructuring with $135M in annual cost savings, and founder Thomas Siebel resumed the CEO role in May 2026. Q1 FY2027 revenue stabilized at $52.4M with bookings up 73% QoQ. Market cap of $1.85B with $651M in cash against $59.5M in debt. Headquartered in Redwood City, California.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): C3.ai successfully pivoted from C3 IoT to an enterprise AI platform company, and the rebrand positioned it at the center of the AI megatrend, but execution has been poor — revenue collapsed 36% from $389M to $250M in FY2026 due to sales restructuring failures and CEO health-related absence [1][3]. The pivot was strategically sound (IoT to AI) but has not yet delivered sustainable growth, and the company is smaller today ($250M revenue) than many AI startups despite a 17-year head start. AI Deployment (1/2): C3.ai IS an AI deployment company — the C3 Agentic AI Platform, C3 AI Studio, C3 Code, and C3 Generative AI represent a comprehensive enterprise AI product suite serving customers including Shell, US Air Force, Koch Industries, and Baker Hughes [2]. However, with revenue declining 36% and the Q3 FY2026 miss attributed to 'sales execution issues,' the deployed products are not achieving market traction at scale, and federal bookings growth of 89% YoY in Q2 has not offset commercial weakness [1]. Market Share (0/2): C3.ai is a marginal participant in enterprise AI with $250M in revenue competing against Microsoft Azure AI ($50B+), AWS AI, Google Cloud AI, Palantir ($2.8B+), and Databricks — the company has been losing ground with a 36% revenue decline while the total enterprise AI market grew 30%+ [1][3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The C3 Agentic AI Platform, C3 Code (auto-generates complete AI applications), and expanded generative AI library represent a technically differentiated product pipeline, with the agentic AI approach aligning with industry direction, but no specific product launches with revenue targets or timelines have been announced. R&D Intensity (1/1): C3.ai invests heavily in R&D as a percentage of revenue — operating expenses far exceed revenue, with the company spending more on R&D and sales than it earns, reflecting top-quartile technology investment intensity for a software company [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): C3.ai's stated vision — to make organizations and society operate more efficiently through enterprise AI — is clear and connects the company's work to a broader purpose of AI-enabled digital transformation [2]. However, the mission is not distinctive in the AI space where every company claims to transform enterprises through AI, and it describes what C3.ai does (sells AI software) rather than articulating a deeper purpose beyond its product. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of significant charitable giving, foundation, or community investment programs for a company with only 764 employees and cumulative net losses exceeding $2B. C3.ai's community impact is limited by its scale and financial losses. Employee Retention (0/2): Major restructuring with $135M in cost savings including significant headcount reductions, CEO health crisis that disrupted operations for months, and a securities class action lawsuit (Liggett Sr. v. C3.ai) alleging misleading statements about CEO health — these factors signal organizational instability rather than a trust-building culture [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful insider buying by Tom Siebel or other executives in the last 12 months; the securities class action creates additional uncertainty around insider sentiment.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock with most metrics at or near floor values. D/E of 8.6% is excellent (score 1.0), reflecting $651M cash against $59.5M debt — the company's strongest financial attribute [1]. ROE of -59.8% is below the 0% floor (score 0.0, 2x weight), reflecting cumulative losses exceeding $2B. Revenue growth YoY of -25.5% is below the -20% floor (score 0.0), as FY2026 revenue collapsed from $389M to $250M due to sales execution failures [1][3]. 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 6.5% scores 0.76 against the 10% target (2x weight), reflecting modest long-term growth from a small base despite the FY2026 collapse. Forward P/E is negative (the company is expected to lose $0.48/share in the forward year), scored at 0.0 as unprofitable companies cannot earn valuation credit. Profit margin of -192.1% is far below the 0% floor (score 0.0), with the company spending roughly $3 for every $1 of revenue. Forward PEG is null and excluded from calculation. Daily dollar volume of $56.8M provides adequate liquidity for a $1.85B market cap.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): C3.ai IS AI infrastructure — the company's entire revenue base ($250M) comes from enterprise AI platform software, agentic AI applications, and generative AI tools, making it structurally immune to AI disruption in the same way that a semiconductor company cannot be disrupted by demand for more computing [2]. The secular trend toward enterprise AI adoption directly benefits C3.ai's addressable market, and Q1 FY2027 bookings surged 73% QoQ as enterprise demand for agentic AI accelerates. Scores 8 rather than 9 because C3.ai's SPECIFIC platform faces competitive displacement risk from vastly larger and better-funded AI platforms operated by Microsoft, Google, AWS, and Palantir — the company's 36% revenue decline in FY2026 demonstrates that being an AI company does not guarantee immunity from competition within the AI industry. AI Opportunity (1/1): C3.ai derives 100% of its revenue from AI products — the C3 Agentic AI Platform, C3 AI Applications, C3 Generative AI, and C3 Code represent a pure-play enterprise AI revenue model with expanding partnerships including Microsoft, AWS, Google Cloud, and McKinsey [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: C3.ai operates with a predominantly finite mindset despite its ambitious AI vision. The company's defining characteristic is founder-CEO Tom Siebel's personal ambition to build 'one of the world's greatest software companies' — a goal framed around company greatness and competitive dominance rather than a cause that transcends the organization. The FY2026 crisis exposed significant organizational fragility: CEO health issues disrupted sales execution, leading to a 36% revenue collapse, $135M restructuring, and a securities class action lawsuit. The company lacks the organizational depth, cultural resilience, and stakeholder trust that infinite game players require to endure through adversity.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): C3.ai's vision is centered on Tom Siebel's ambition to build 'one of the world's greatest software companies' through enterprise AI — a goal that is fundamentally self-referential and finite [2]. While the company's products serve meaningful use cases (energy optimization, defense readiness, supply chain efficiency), the articulated cause is about corporate greatness rather than advancing a future state that benefits others. Siebel's comparison to his prior work at Oracle and Siebel Systems frames the endeavor as personal legacy-building rather than a purpose that inspires sacrifice from stakeholders.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): C3.ai's organizational environment shows significant trust deficits. CEO Siebel's health crisis directly disrupted sales operations, revealing dangerous single-point-of-failure leadership dependency [1][3]. The subsequent $135M restructuring included substantial layoffs, the securities class action (Liggett Sr. v. C3.ai) alleges management misled investors about CEO health, and the company has cycled through leadership — Siebel returned as CEO in May 2026 after stepping back. With only 764 employees and a culture reportedly centered on Siebel's personal directives, the organization lacks the distributed leadership and psychological safety that Sinek's Circle of Safety requires.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Siebel's competitive posture positions C3.ai as a unique and superior enterprise AI platform rather than acknowledging the strengths of competitors like Palantir, Microsoft, or Databricks [2]. The company's messaging emphasizes its 'first mover' status in enterprise AI and Siebel's track record at Oracle/Siebel Systems rather than engaging with competitors' advantages as motivation for improvement. No evidence of management publicly citing rivals' strengths or using competitive dynamics as a learning mechanism.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): C3.ai has demonstrated meaningful strategic pivots — from C3 Energy (2009) to C3 IoT (2016) to C3 AI (2019) to C3 Agentic AI (2025) — each repositioning the platform toward the highest-growth technology trend [2]. The most recent pivot to agentic AI aligns with industry direction and shows willingness to evolve the product. However, these pivots are incremental rebrandings of the same core platform technology rather than transformative reinventions, and the FY2026 revenue collapse suggests the pivots have not yet achieved sustainable product-market fit.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): C3.ai's leadership has not demonstrated the pattern of costly long-term bets that Sinek's framework requires. The FY2026 restructuring was reactive survival — cutting $135M in costs and headcount after a 36% revenue collapse — rather than proactive investment in future capability [1][3]. Siebel's return as CEO in May 2026 was necessitated by the crisis he partly caused through his health-related absence, not a courageous strategic decision. The company has accumulated over $2B in cumulative losses without achieving sustainable profitability, which reflects persistent money-burning rather than disciplined long-term investment.

investment_thesis: C3.ai at $11.53 with a $1.85B market cap is a pure-play enterprise AI platform company trading at a deep discount after a difficult FY2026 — revenue collapsed 36% to $250.3M due to sales execution failures and CEO health issues, but Q1 FY2027 shows stabilization at $52.4M with bookings surging 73% QoQ as founder Tom Siebel resumed the CEO role [1]. The balance sheet provides a floor valuation: $651M in cash against $59.5M in debt gives a net cash position of $592M, representing 32% of market cap. The $135M restructuring should improve the path to profitability, free cash flow turned slightly positive at $2.1M in Q1 FY2027, and the strategic pivot to agentic AI positions C3.ai in the fastest-growing segment of enterprise software with partnerships spanning Microsoft, AWS, Google Cloud, and McKinsey [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is existential. FY2026 revenue of $250.3M represented a 36% decline from $389M, with Q3 FY2026 revenue missing guidance by 25%+ ($53.3M actual vs. $72-80M guided), and analysts project a further 10% decline in FY2027 [3]. The GAAP operating loss exceeded $465M on $250M in revenue, meaning the company spent roughly $3 for every $1 earned. The securities class action (Liggett Sr. v. C3.ai) alleging misleading statements about CEO health creates legal overhang and governance questions. C3.ai competes against Microsoft Azure AI, AWS AI, Google Cloud AI, Palantir, and Databricks — all vastly larger and better-funded — and the 36% revenue decline occurred during a period when the enterprise AI market grew 30%+, indicating C3.ai is losing share to these competitors [1][3]. With only 764 employees and significant founder dependency, the company lacks the organizational scale and resilience to compete in a market dominated by trillion-dollar technology platforms.
key_catalysts: Agentic AI platform repositioning — the pivot to agentic AI aligns with the highest-growth segment of enterprise software, and Q1 FY2027 bookings up 73% QoQ suggest early traction in the post-restructuring commercial strategy under Siebel's direct leadership [1]

Net cash position of $592M ($651M cash less $59.5M debt) represents 32% of market cap, providing multi-year runway and a floor valuation — the company cannot go bankrupt in the near term, giving Siebel time to execute the turnaround [1]

Cost restructuring of $135M annually with free cash flow turning positive in Q1 FY2027 — if revenue stabilizes at the $52M quarterly run rate ($208M annualized) while costs are being cut, the path to breakeven narrows significantly [1]
key_risks: Revenue collapse may not be over — FY2026 revenue declined 36% to $250.3M while the broader enterprise AI market grew 30%+, indicating C3.ai is losing competitive share to Microsoft, AWS, Google, and Palantir, and analysts project a further 10% revenue decline in FY2027 [1][3]

Founder dependency and governance risk — the 36% revenue collapse was directly attributed to CEO Siebel's health-related absence from sales operations, and the securities class action (Liggett Sr. v. C3.ai) alleges management misled investors about this risk, creating both operational and legal overhang [3]

Unsustainable operating model — GAAP operating losses exceeding $465M on $250M in revenue mean the company is burning through its $651M cash reserve, and if the turnaround fails, the cash cushion provides only 2-3 years of runway at current burn rates [1][3]
